title: Stop the price import from hiding its own failures

blocks.text: Every night a job imports the suppliers' price lists into the catalog. Its report counts the rows it turned away, and the buyers call suppliers about them. Two things went wrong last month. A supplier renamed a column in its file, the report said every one of its 3,000 rows was rejected, and the buyers spent a morning on the phone over a file that had no typo in it. And a deploy that interrupted the job did not stop it: it counted the rest of the file as rejected and finished.

Finish the `TODO` in `importRow(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/PriceImport.java`. A row whose price is not a whole number of cents is turned away and counted, as before. A file the job can't read at all fails the import, and an interrupt ends it with the `InterruptedException` that `importAll` declares, so the job runner sees it. About six lines in total.
The tests hand the job a throttle that never waits but can be interrupted on a chosen call.

cases.says: rows with a whole number of cents go into the catalog, spaces around the number allowed, and rows with any other price are counted as rejected
a file whose price column is missing makes the import fail instead of rejecting every row
an interrupt while waiting for the throttle ends the import with InterruptedException, and no later row is written

origin.section: A catch Clause Catches Its Type and Every Subtype

concepts: catch (Exception) around a blocking call also catches InterruptedException, so a thread that was asked to stop carries on.
A catch clause takes its type and every subtype, so catch (Exception) around a parse also turns a bug such as a NullPointerException into the fallback.
